original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: On the single length-42 floor word recorded in PR #7016, classify every pair 0 <= s <= t <= 41 and list the nonzero binary masks of weight other than 3 that q_s + q_t does not realize. The weight-3 gap of that same word is a control, not a new exchange bound.
scope_change_reason: The catalogue card asks for one new connector operation. This package keeps the unsigned dirty connector alphabet fixed and answers open question 2 of PR #7016: which non-weight-3 masks the recorded witness misses. A new operation is not the missing step.
bottleneck_link: Side result on the recursive-interface schedule. A depth-two block needs every nonzero mask, so the weight-3 count on this word cannot by itself be a block. No supplier, consumer, or selected kappa changes.
stop_rule: Stop once all 903 pairs on this word are classified and the non-weight-3 missing set is listed. Stop without a substitute if the word's weight-3 missing set is not exactly (1, 3, 5).
evidence: Exhaustive finite census of the 903 pairs 0 <= s <= t <= 41 on the recorded word. The allowed-set reading and the mod-7 reading agree on every pair. The word realizes 41 of 43 nonzero masks of weight other than 3. The missing masks are (3, 5) and (0, 1, 3, 5). The same census misses the recorded weight-3 mask (1, 3, 5). Eight pairs realize the zero vector. Boundary 42 adds no nonzero mask. Seven controls cover the floor word, the two readings, the weight identity, three hand-checked prefixes, the {3, 5} superset corollary, one adjacent transposition, and one rejected call-count edit. This is not an unrestricted nonexistence claim.

open_questions.question: Can one explicit six-source length-42 floor word, other than the recorded #7016 witness, realize both non-weight-3 masks (3, 5) and (0, 1, 3, 5)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A depth-two block needs both masks. This census shows the recorded witness misses both. One other word that realizes both would separate that miss from the floor-word hypotheses. An exhaustive census of every floor word would be a different claim.
open_questions.first_step: Evaluate the same 903-pair predicate on one other concrete length-42 floor word and record, for these two masks only, whether each is realized.
open_questions.blocked_by: Only the recorded witness is enumerated here, and no second characteristic-7 floor word is certified in this package. The two-pair weight-3 exchange remains open question 1 of PR #7016.
